profile.reading:
Per NTT's own Global Data Centers facility page, this building, NTT Ashburn VA7, is located at 44371 Gigabit Plaza, Ashburn, VA 20147, on NTT's 224-megawatt, 78-acre Ashburn campus in Loudoun County's "Data Center Alley." The operator publishes nearly 125,000 square feet of data floor space and 36 megawatts of critical IT load, delivered as N+1 distributed redundancy across 6-megawatt vaults; unlike NTT's earlier Ashburn buildings, VA7 was not yet operational as of this registry's research, with NTT's own page stating availability from September 2026.

Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility, including new-build capacity like VA7 coming online in 2026. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that will raise a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers effective January 1, 2027; data center customers with 25 megawatts or more of demand, a threshold VA7 exceeds on its own, must sign 14-year mandatory contracts and pay a minimum 85% of transmission and distribution costs and a minimum 60% of generation costs regardless of actual usage, per Inside Climate News's reporting on the SCC decision.

NTT's US Global Data Centers footprint spans seven named campuses in total: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts; Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts; Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts; Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts; Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts; and a combined Sacramento/Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts, totaling roughly 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity, per the operator's own locations page. The US business operates under the NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas name, the successor brand to RagingWire Data Centers, now under Japan's NTT DATA Group and parent Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed company not subject to SEC 10-K filing requirements.

reading.body:
NTT VA7 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 125,000 square feet of technical space in Ashburn, Virginia, placing it twelfth among the nineteen Virginia facilities that disclose power figures publicly.

Power density at VA7 is roughly 288 watts per square foot of technical space. This density sits between enterprise and hyperscale workload profiles. At 40 kW per rack, typical of AI training, 36 MW supports approximately 900 racks. At 10 kW per rack, common in legacy enterprise deployments, the same power supports around 3,600 racks. The operator has not published rack count, cooling architecture, or power usage effectiveness, so which density class this facility actually operates at remains unknown from the disclosed data.

Among Virginia's 326 mapped data center facilities, only 19 publish megawatt figures. The nineteen publishing sites declare 1,326 MW combined, meaning VA7's share is 2.7 percent. Ashburn hosts the densest concentration of data center capacity in Virginia and ranks among the densest markets globally. The remaining 307 facilities in the state have disclosed no capacity figures this source has retrieved, so the true distribution of power and the actual rank of VA7 within all Virginia facilities cannot be determined.
